correctness.rationale: On the part-constant invariant subspace T=D^{-1}A is the exact row-stochastic quotient P=alpha beta^T-diag(theta) with theta_i=n_i/(N-n_i). The positive diagonal similarity diag(sqrt(n_i(N-n_i))) yields a real symmetric matrix. Each repeated-size pole has eigenspace consisting of zero-sum coordinates on that group, and the monotone secular equation gives exactly one simple nonpole eigenvalue per distinct size, with eigenvectors nonzero in every part. Vandermonde separation over k consecutive times proves necessity and sufficiency of the sensor criterion. Minimum sensors and counts follow by choosing all but one part in each repeated-size class. The single-sensor determinant follows by a monic-polynomial recurrence in the k-1 off-j nodes -theta_i; the product is an exact Vandermonde determinant. The embedded CHECK.py uses exact fractions and independently tests quotient ranks, determinant, minimal cardinality and counts in 15,308 assertions; those bounded checks are not presented as an infinite proof. The determinant is not claimed as a smallest-singular-value formula.

originality.rationale: The 2017 finite-dimensional dynamical sampling spectral projection test is acknowledged and not presented as new. The 2018/2020 cograph controllability results concern combinatorial full-Laplacian dynamics and different observed state dimensions; their theorems do not evaluate the present part-constant random-walk quotient Krylov determinant. The 2026 motivating paper discusses normalized-Laplacian graph band sampling and finite path experiments; its abstract does not state the exact multipartite placement/count/volume formula, but inaccessible full text remains a material novelty risk. Actual published-finding corpus searches returned cycle/path observability and unrelated complete multipartite combinatorics, no explicit implication. The new assertion is the complete all-part-size placement and physical-sensor count together with a sharp k-by-k Krylov-volume product, rather than the generic PBH or Vandermonde test.

value.rationale: Repeated equal-size graph communities create exact eigenvalue multiplicity barriers under repeated random-walk measurements. For every part profile the result identifies a minimal, physically implementable sensor budget and counts all optimal vertex placements; the exact one-sensor Krylov determinant captures a nontrivial conditioning-volume invariant that vanishes precisely at community-size collisions. This distinguishes one-sensor recovery from unavoidable multichannel sensing, solves a natural complete graph-family sampling-design problem, and is not a routine unmotivated parameter slice. Scope excludes within-community modes and claims no minimum singular value.
